input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives us (Sparkling) an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement at any time on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge. Section 17 otherwise confers termination rights only for insolvency events or uncured material default (17(c)), and no provision anywhere in the Agreement (including the maintenance terms in Section 10, which run for renewable one-year terms) lets Garman terminate for convenience. The clause therefore sits at the playbook fallback: customer convenience termination on 90 days' notice (preferred is 30 days), no termination fee, and no vendor convenience right at all — better than the fallback on the vendor side. The only sub-element short of the preferred position is the absence of an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (a refund appears only for termination due to Garman's default under 17(c)); we note this rather than redline it, and can raise the 30-day notice period and refund mechanic as a non-essential commercial ask if the negotiation reopens Section 17.
